source_review.notes: Reviewed current Abseil Swiss-table design and raw_hash_set source, official Go Swiss-map explanation and current runtime source, current CPython dictobject.c, current Folly F14 design, current Rust HashMap documentation and hashbrown implementation repository, current LLVM DenseMap source, and current ISO C++ unordered-container requirements. All ten final destinations returned HTTP 200. Layout descriptions, API contracts, implementation constants, and benchmark statements are scoped to their named sources and current versions.

evidence: Checked n,m,alpha,H,C(m),S,I,p,E,P,usable(node),live/fill,slack,fragmentation,owned,retained,process,peak,tag, and width-transition notation.
Checked that inline, indexed-packed, vector-indexed, and node allocation terms are kept structurally distinct.
Checked every bytes-per-live-entry use names a nonzero live denominator and a scoped numerator.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Equations are deliberately simplified representation models; actual source layouts and allocators may add, combine, or round regions differently.

evidence: Recomputed flat bytes at n=80,m=128: header 48 + aligned control 144 + slots 128*16=2048, total 2240 and 28.00 per live entry.
Recomputed indexed bytes: header 48 + 128 one-byte indices + 80*24 packed entries=1920, total 2096 and 26.20 per live entry.
Recomputed node bytes: header 48 + 128*8 bucket pointers=1024 + 80*32 rounded nodes=2560, total 3632 and 45.40 per live entry.
Recomputed destination flat bytes at m=256 as 48+272+4096=4416 and old-plus-new growth peak as 2240+4416=6656.
Confirmed flat empty-slot payload slack is (128-80)*16=768 bytes under the named model.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Totals exclude allocator headers/arena fragmentation, transitive payload objects, process/runtime metadata, concurrency state, and temporary move/callback storage exactly as labeled.

evidence: Verified B_flat=H+align(C(m))+mS, B_indexed=H+align(mI)+pE, and B_node=H+align(mP)+sum usable(node_j) match their described layouts.
Verified increasing alpha reduces inline slack approximately by S per newly occupied slot but does not alone bound probes, fill, tombstones, or adversarial work.
Verified growth peak requires simultaneously live generations and is not derivable from destination steady-state bytes alone.
Verified a short tag only filters candidates and full equality remains necessary for semantic correctness.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No closed-form probe, cache, allocator fragmentation, or optimal-layout theorem is asserted.

evidence: Reviewed empty denominator, one/tiny map, inline promotion, minimum group, threshold-minus/plus, pre/post growth, reserve error, deletion/tombstones, shrink, clear, maximum capacity, and growth peak.
Reviewed large/aligned/nontrivial payloads, indirect strings, cached hashes, node pools, packed holes, compaction, stable references, insertion order, and borrowed lookup.
Reviewed signed/sentinel index limits, widening, offset ranges, checked byte arithmetic, allocation/hash/equality/move failure, initialization/drop exactly once, and corrupt physical input.
Reviewed hostile hashes/tags, repeated cleanup/growth, untrusted capacity metadata, memory exhaustion, shards/skew, readers/retired generations, NUMA, and allocator/runtime variation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Tiny-map and width-transition choices require distribution- and implementation-specific evidence rather than a universal threshold.

evidence: Checked FULL metadata identifies exactly one initialized live payload; EMPTY/DELETED exposes none; size/fill/deleted/growth counts agree.
Checked fingerprints select candidates only, indices/offsets stay representable and reference valid dense entries, and reverse mappings update on compaction.
Checked insert, erase, clear, promote, compact, widen, grow, shrink, publish, and retire preserve exact logical content and payload lifetime.
Checked iterator/reference/handle behavior is derived from flat, node, or packed storage rather than implied by the map abstraction.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable code models allocation arithmetic only and does not implement these operational invariants.

evidence: Reviewed the ledger proof that each direct representation region is included once and excluded transitive/runtime terms are named separately.
Reviewed candidate filtering, probe termination state, failure-atomic publication, exact destruction, compaction reverse update, and widening obligations.
Reviewed constrained optimization framing: memory/peak is minimized only subject to latency, stability, order, failure, concurrency, and adversarial requirements.
Reviewed why independent implementation accounting plus allocator/process measurement is needed to explain rather than hide discrepancies.
proof_review.notes: No named production implementation is claimed to use the executable constants or the simplified formulas without additional terms.

evidence: Abseil, Go, CPython, Folly, Rust/hashbrown, LLVM, and ISO C++ observations are scoped to current official design, source, or API surfaces.
Requested, aligned, allocator-usable, owned, retained, resident, committed, and peak bytes are distinguished throughout.
Final-state, growth-peak, exact arithmetic, expected filtering, latency, stability, and empirical performance claims are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Current implementation constants and policies may change and are not promoted into portable language guarantees.

evidence: The standard-library Python accounting trace passed exact ten-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the recorded toolchain.
It emits evidence=finite_layout_accounting_model and explicitly prints excluded=allocator_metadata_and_transitive_payloads.
All ten final source destinations and all repository-local links were checked directly.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real allocation, ABI sizeof/alignment, allocator usable size, RSS, cache/TLB, latency, named hash-map implementation, hostile workload, failure injection, concurrency, or benchmark was empirically measured.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed memory scopes, layout equations, active metadata, load/slack, inline/node/packed payloads, dense iteration, tiny maps, growth peak, lifetime/failure, concurrency, security, measurement reconciliation, and decision evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed checked reserve/capacity/byte/index arithmetic, allocator rounding and fragmentation, payload ownership, stability matrices, promotion/compaction/widening, shrink hysteresis, peak admission, sharding/retirement, typed failures, untrusted serialization, instrumentation, lifecycle sampling, and raw benchmark artifacts.

pedagogical_review.notes: Builds from a scoped memory ledger to layout mechanisms and production constraints, compares five current implementation strategies without declaring a universal winner, includes a reproduced arithmetic model, twelve causal misconceptions, ten examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary-source, mathematical, executable-snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Abseil/Go/CPython/Folly/Rust/hashbrown/LLVM/runtime maintainer, allocator, performance, security, reliability, operations, architecture, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite accounting model prove neither any named implementation's footprint, ABI/allocator/process memory, transitive retention, cache or latency superiority, universal minimum bytes per entry, optimal load/growth policy, generic exception/lifetime safety, hash-flood immunity, concurrent linearizability, safe reclamation, benchmark superiority, certification, nor deployment fitness.
